lines: The app ships no composer/autoload.php, so the server registers its generic loader for lib/ and looks every class up in the file system.

A composer/composer.json with config.vendor-dir ".", config.optimize-autoloader true, a config.autoloader-suffix and autoload.psr-4 {"OCA\\gov_file_drop\\": "../lib/"} makes composer dump-autoload write composer/autoload.php with a class map; the code of the app does not change.
3 uses of the private API of the server in 1 file. Only OCP and NCU are public: what is below OC changes without notice between majors.

1 class implements or extends what the public API marks #[Consumable] in a major of Nextcloud 27 to 36: an app calls it, and the server may add a method to it in any release, which breaks a class that implements it.

lines: 1 use in 1 file of the public API that the oldest majors of Nextcloud 27 to 36 do not have yet. Either min-version in appinfo/info.xml goes up, or the app does without it there.

3 inline scripts in templates/. The Content Security Policy of the server runs neither a <script> without a source or the nonce of the response nor an event handler attribute, so the browser does not run them. A script added with OCP\Util::addScript() or addInitScript() runs.

lines: 1 use in 1 file of the public API that is deprecated in Nextcloud 27 to 36. The text of the tag names the replacement where it has one.
lib/Provider/GovPublicShareTemplateProvider.php:46 OCP\Constants::PERMISSION_CREATE: deprecated since Nextcloud 13; Use \OCP\Constants::PERMISSION_CREATE instead

15 inline styles in templates/. The default Content Security Policy of the server allows inline style; a response whose policy disallows it drops them. A stylesheet added with OCP\Util::addStyle() holds in both cases.
